svg.text: Clarify what the buyer means before you change price, scope, timing, or boundaries.
FICTIONAL SUMMIT AIR AND HEAT COMPLETED MODEL

g.text: Buyer exact words
“That’s almost twice what the other developer is talking about.”
What is already known
Alex stated $9,000–$12,000 territory. Another provider is discussing a roughly
$5,000 visual rebuild. Eric owns the spend decision.
Possible meanings
Hard affordability; perceived equivalence; weak value; approval concern;
or the cheaper option may genuinely fit better.
Neutral clarification
“Is the issue that Summit cannot approve an investment in this territory, or that
the two approaches still look like they are solving essentially the same thing?”
Buyer clarification
There is no hard $5,000 ceiling. Eric does not want to pay nearly double
for what he still perceives as “a prettier website.”
Actual issue
Understanding: perceived equivalence between a broader engagement and a visual rebuild.
Appropriate response
Compare only known obligations. Reconnect the broader work to publishing control,
campaign/measurement needs, ServiceTitan continuity, and regional positioning.
Next decision
Finish the remaining pre-proposal conditions, then run the Proposal Readiness Gate.

svg.text: DO NOT ANSWER THE INTERPRETATION YOU INVENTED
No reflex discount. No competitor attack. No invented ROI. Diagnose first.
